summary: When attaching seven candles from a lit stack, JavaScript stops in end_burn because the split child has no BURN_OBJECT timer. C mkobj.c:splitobj calls timeout.c:obj_split_timers for every timed source object before duplicating light sources. JavaScript splitobj currently records that void timer-copy callee as unported, so the candle child is lit but has no burn timer.

source.branch: After copying an object stack, splitobj resets child.timed and child.lamplit, updates parent/child ownership chains, then calls timeout.c:obj_split_timers when the source is timed. That helper copies every TIMER_OBJECT timer from source to child at the same remaining expiry before light.c:obj_split_light_source runs.
callers: The direct C caller of timeout.c:obj_split_timers is mkobj.c:splitobj. Runtime reaches it through apply.c:use_candle while attaching seven candles to a candelabrum; existing splitobj production callers all use the common JavaScript function.
dependencies: timeout.c:obj_split_timers calls start_timer and discards its return; start_timer is implemented in js/timeout.js.
mkobj.c:splitobj calls obj_split_timers and discards its void result. JavaScript retains an explicit splitObjectTimers hook and uses the source implementation in ordinary gameplay.

selectionReason: Selected the officially admitted v79 lit-candle case after the unchanged-input replay matched 235 screens, cursors, and 2564 RNG calls, then stopped at step 235 with end_burn: lit object has no burn timer. Prep source trace points to mkobj.c:splitobj omitting timeout.c:obj_split_timers in active JS gameplay.
evidence: The v79 accepted-boundary prefix matches screens, cursors, and RNG through step 234, then step 235 triggers the exact end_burn missing timer error.

C splitobj calls obj_split_timers before obj_split_light_source whenever obj->timed is nonzero. timeout.c:obj_split_timers iterates the timer queue, saves next_timer before insertion, and starts a matching TIMER_OBJECT timer on dest with curr->timeout minus current moves.

JavaScript js/obj.js:splitobj currently calls an optional splitObjectTimers hook; with no hook it records note_unported("timeout.c obj_split_timers"), so a lit candle split keeps the light but loses the timer.
